_about: Narrative summaries for the Position Intel sentiment table, written from web coverage on 15 Oct 2026. scripts/fetch-sentiment.cjs merges these with the fetched numbers; update them when you re-run after new events.

NVDA.summary: Nvidia hit record highs in early October and neared a $6 trillion market value after a $150 billion buyback, with management guiding Q3 revenue to about $108 billion on the Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin ramp. The past week turned risk-off: a hotter CPI print hit chip stocks and NVDA fell 3.2% on 14 Oct to $221.30, about 9% below its 52-week high. The one-month tone stays constructive (33 Buy ratings, no Sell); the one-week read is pulled down by price momentum, not by company news.

MSFT.summary: Microsoft closed at its first record high in about a year on 13 Oct, up more than 50% from its June low, as Azure passed $100 billion in annual revenue and grew 43% last quarter with an $678 billion commercial backlog. Jefferies lifted its target to $650. The debate is now whether Azure can hold above 40% growth (guide 44-45% cc) when Microsoft reports on 28 Oct; routine CFO plan sales drew little reaction. Note this is more upbeat than the thesis-drift row's 'Azure decel' read.

CRM.summary: Salesforce rallied in the past week after BofA double-upgraded the stock to Buy (target $285 from $160), arguing agentic AI deepens lock-in rather than eroding seats; Agentforce ARR is now above $1.5 billion. Dreamforce brought AIforce and the Koa reasoning model built with Nvidia, but no new Agentforce pricing. The one-month picture is mixed: shares are still down about 8% on the month and trail the market in 2026, and Oppenheimer's survey points to healthy spending rather than accelerating demand.

UNH.summary: UnitedHealth beat Q3 on 13 Oct with adjusted EPS of $4.69 against about $4.12 expected, and raised 2026 guidance to at least $20.50, its third increase this year. The medical care ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9%, helped partly by $610 million of favourable reserve development. Shares rose 4.8% on 14 Oct while the market sold off, and coverage frames it as the margin-repair story gaining credibility. Watch how much of the MCR gain is one-off reserve releases.
